gaps.note: The guide gives a typical and maximum draw per module and no figure for the chassis itself; the chassis total is whatever its occupants sum to. Each line card carries its own typical and maximum draw, so a loaded chassis's total is the sum of its occupants; none is written here.
gaps.wanted: a chassis-level draw from Cisco, or confirmation that the sum of the module table is the answer

gaps.note: Which fabric module each line card goes with, and how many are needed, is listed here and NOT ENFORCED: no bay or card restricts the fabric module it is seated with. The guide's Overview Table 1 (PDF pp8-9, printed 2-3) pairs the cards modelled here with the N9K-C9508-FM-E, -FM-E2 and -FM-G; the count is the fabric modules required for maximum bandwidth, read by line order. N9K-X9736C-FX: FM-E 5, FM-E2 5, FM-G 5. N9K-X97160YC-EX: FM-E 4, FM-E2 4, FM-G 4. N9K-X9732C-FX: FM-E 4 plus 1 for redundancy, FM-E2 4 plus 1 for redundancy, FM-G 4. N9K-X9716D-GX: FM-G 4 only. The guide's notes: all fabric modules in the switch must be of one type; with the -FM-G the empty slots take N9K-C9508-FAN-PWR and the N9K-C9508-FAN2 fan trays are used; and "Do not mix ACI-mode line cards with NX-OS mode line cards in the same switch" (PDF p7, printed 1). "Migrate the switch to 400-Gigabit -GX line cards" (PDF p114, printed 108) says to replace the older fabric modules with N9K-C9508-FM-G modules.
gaps.wanted: a restriction in the format between a card and the fabric modules it is seated with

gaps.note: The clearance figure (PDF p24, callout 14) gives the width of the chassis plus the vertical mounting brackets as 19.2 in (48.8 cm). The ear model has no field for an overall width, so the mounting-bracket region is not sized by it and the front face stays the 444.5 mm chassis width.
gaps.wanted: ear support for an overall width, or a dimensioned front view of the bracket

gaps.note: The guide has no flat front or rear elevation, and the NetBox elevations are not held. Every position on both faces is derived from the dimension table and the arrangement in the isometric figures; see the front-stack and rear-stack provenance. No position is measured.
gaps.wanted: a flat front and rear elevation of the chassis with dimensions, or the NetBox elevation images

gaps.note: The guide says a blank module sits in an empty supervisor or system-controller slot ("remove the blank module that is already in that slot. Unscrew its captive screw") and gives it no part number, drawing or dimension. The supervisor and system-controller bays therefore show nothing when empty.
gaps.wanted: the part number and a drawing of the supervisor and system-controller slot blanks

gaps.note: The bay sizes are the module envelopes of the dimension table, and the positions are the stack derived from them; none is a measurement of the chassis. The fan-tray bays and the fabric-module bays occupy the same area of the rear face because the fabric modules are behind the fan trays.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear view with the fan trays removed

gaps.note: The side and top faces are named in the figures (handles on both sides, mounting bracket, rack rail positions) and no figure dimensions any feature on them, so those faces carry regions with no coordinates. The bottom face is empty: no view of it is published.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned side and top view

airflow.note: datasheet - "Air intake from the cold aisle for all modules and power supplies" and "Air exhaust to the hot aisle" (clearance figure, callouts 4 and 5), and "port-side intake airflow" for every supply. The chassis is front-to-back.

chassis.note: datasheet - Appendix A "Switch Dimensions" (printed p113, PDF p119): "Cisco N9508 chassis: width 17.5 inches (44.5 cm); depth 31.76 inches (80.67 cm) for chassis and handles; height 22.70 inches (57.78 cm) (13 RU)". Modelled as 444.5 x 577.85 x 806.7 mm. CONFLICT ON HEIGHT: 22.70 in is 576.6 mm, but the same cell gives 57.78 cm, the rack-requirements text gives "13-RU (22.7 inches or 57.8 cm)", the bottom-rail step gives "13 RU (22.75 in [57.8 cm])", and 13 x 44.45 mm is 577.85 mm. 22.70 reads as a rounding slip for 22.75; 577.85 is used, which is also what the front stack of modules adds up to. CONFLICT ON DEPTH: the clearance figure (PDF p24, callout 11) gives the chassis depth as 33.15 in (84.2 cm); the table's 31.76 in (80.67 cm) is used because it is the stated dimension "for chassis and handles", and the figure's number is not explained.

ears-and-kits.note: drawing - the clearance figure (PDF p24) shows the chassis between front and rear vertical rack posts with its front at the front posts; the front figure (PDF p11, callout 5) shows "2 vertical mounting brackets that are used to mount the chassis onto rack" at the sides of the front. The shipped position is therefore flush, and no `at` is written: no figure gives the bracket's depth position. The clearance figure (PDF p24, callout 14) prints "Width of the chassis plus vertical mounting brackets on each side" as 19.2 in (48.8 cm), against the 17.5 in chassis: about 21.6 mm of bracket on each side. The ear model takes a depth offset and a height and no width, so that span is carried here and in a gap, not drawn. A rear-mount position is not given by the guide. The bottom-support rails (kit N9K-C9500-RMK; the accessory kit is N9K-ACC-KIT in the procedure and N9K-C9500-ACK in its table) carry the weight; the rack must be a four-post rack 24 to 32 in deep between rails. No kit is listed under `chassis.kits`: the first `kind: kit` contract in the library broke six existing tests, so the kit is left out of this batch.

fabric-slots.note: datasheet - "Overview" note: three fabric modules go in FM 2, 4 and 6; four in FM 2, 3, 4 and 6; five in FM 2 to 6; six in FM 1 to 6. Slots left empty take N9K-C9508-FAN-PWR (with -FM-G and N9K-C9508-FAN2) or, with any other fabric module, a blank by slot: an empty odd slot (FM 1, FM 3, FM 5) takes N9K-C9508-FM-CV (Overview note, PDF p10; migration cautions, PDF pp113-116), and an empty even slot (FM 2, FM 4, FM 6) takes N9K-C9508-FM-Z, which powers the fan tray (Fan Tray LEDs, PDF p135). Table 1 (PDF p7) lists only the FM-Z in its blank column. With N9K-C9508-FM-R2 no fabric slot may be empty. A bay holds any of them; the pairing rules are the guide's and are not enforced by the model.

front-stack.note: estimated - every position on the front is derived, not measured. The guide has no flat front view: its front figure (PDF p11) is an isometric drawing. The layout follows that figure's arrangement and the guide's dimension table: a top band for the chassis lamps; eight line cards of 1.75 in (44.45 mm) stacked top to bottom; the two supervisors, 1.75 in high and 8.0 in (203.2 mm) wide with brackets, side by side; and eight power supplies standing on end, 5.25 in (133.35 mm) tall and 1.75 in (44.45 mm) wide, in a row at the bottom. The top band is the remainder, 44.45 mm, which is also what the figure suggests. The cage is taken as the 17.0 in (431.8 mm) line-card width, centred in the 444.5 mm face. The power supplies are spread across the 431.8 mm cage at an even 53.975 mm pitch. Overlaying the figure is not possible: it is perspective, so no aspect check (Gate 1) can be made.

lifecycle.note: datasheet - Cisco's support page lists the Nexus 9508 as available (support page "Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switches", https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/switches/nexus-9000-series-switches/series.html). Sale status of each module is per module: N9K-SUP-A, N9K-SUP-B, N9K-C9508-FM, -FM-S and -FM-E are end-of-sale by notice; the others have no status on the support page and are recorded as unknown.

line-cards.note: datasheet - the eight line-card slots accept the line-card blank N9K-C9500-LC-CV and the line cards this guide supports among those modelled: N9K-X9736C-FX, N9K-X97160YC-EX, N9K-X9732C-FX and N9K-X9716D-GX, which Overview Table 1 and the power tables (PDF pp8-9 and 18-19, printed 2-3 and 12-13) list. A line card is accepted because this chassis's own guide supports it. The other 9500 line cards follow in later batches; the N9K-X9788TC-FX is listed in the guide and not modelled, because the guides name its 48 ports three ways and no figure of its faceplate is held. The guide's weights section (PDF p120, printed 114) has a heading and no table, so no line-card weight is read from this guide.

power-slots.note: datasheet - "Installing or Replacing Power Supplies": with n+n redundancy the supplies in slots 1 to 4 go to one source and those in slots 5 to 8 to the other. Any supply type may be mixed ("The switch can be powered by a mix of AC, DC, HVAC/HVDC power sources" in the Overview; "Do not use a mix of AC and DC power sources" in the power-requirements text: the guide contradicts itself, and every type is accepted by every slot).

rear-stack.note: estimated - the rear is derived the same way. The guide's rear figure (PDF p12) is isometric. Three fan trays of 5.04 in (128.02 mm) are centred across the width, each 18.08 in (459.2 mm) tall with its brackets; the six fabric modules, 2.46 in (62.48 mm) wide, sit behind them on a pitch of half a fan tray, so FM 1 and FM 2 are behind FAN 1, FM 3 and FM 4 behind FAN 2, FM 5 and FM 6 behind FAN 3 (the guide says the even-numbered fabric slot is the one behind a fan tray that powers it). The two system controllers, 7.81 in (198.37 mm) wide with brackets and 1.42 in (36.07 mm) high, sit below the fan trays. The vertical position of the controllers and the margin above the fan trays are estimated.

ru.note: datasheet - 13 RU, printed in the dimensions table and in "Rack and Cabinet Requirements". Chassis weight: the guide's weights table is empty in the held copy; "up to 395 pounds (179 kg) when fully loaded" is stated in "Installing a Chassis in a Rack or Cabinet" and is carried as an attribute, not as the chassis weight.

slots.note: datasheet - "Overview": supervisor modules in slots SUP 1 and SUP 2 (modules 27 and 28), system controllers in SC 1 and SC 2 (modules 29 and 30), line cards in LC 1 to LC 8 (modules 1 to 8, top to bottom), fabric modules in FM 1 to FM 6 (slots 21 to 26, left to right), fan trays in FAN 1 to FAN 3 and power supplies in PS 1 to PS 8 (left to right). Numbering is the guide's; whether each label is printed on the metal is not shown by any figure the guide gives.

sources.note: Cisco N9508 NX-OS Mode Switch Hardware Installation Guide (140 pp; first published 2014-11-21, last modified 2026-09-17), https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/datacenter/nexus9000/hw/n9508_hig/guide/b_n9508_nxos-mode_hardware_install_guide.pdf (page numbers below are PDF pages, and the printed page is six lower). Cisco's Nexus 9504 and 9516 hardware installation guides were read to confirm that the supervisors, the system controller and the 3000 W supplies are the same parts. The NetBox devicetype-library file for N9K-C9508 (u_height 13) and its elevation images were NOT available to this work - only a path listing of that library is - so no NetBox elevation was compared. No data sheet, photograph, 3D model or stencil is held for the 9508.
